messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: unusual-auth-surge detected in prod-inference (inference-ws) — region: eu-west-2. 1200 failed auth attempts then 230 successful with short-lived tokens. Alert id=INC-2026-0421-77

incident-bot: Related telemetry: spike in ws-requests, repeated header shapes: 'Authorization: Bearer <token_fragment>'. Suspected log leakage path: inference-ws debug logging rollout 2026-04-21T11:02Z.

maria_oncall: I'm on it. Acknowledge. Triage lead: alice_sre, security: sam_security. Rachel, please standby for customer-impact sync.

alice_sre: looking at ws pods now. `kubectl -n inference get pods | grep ws` shows rolling pods with recent env LOG_LEVEL=debug pushed 11:00Z.

alice_sre: tailing logs:
```
[DEBUG] 2026-04-21T11:03:10Z req_id=abc123 path=/v1/generate auth_header="Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...snip"
```
Looks like the debug formatter prints partial Authorization header into debug logs for a subset of requests.

sam_security: :lock: do NOT delete logs. Preserve a copy (s3://redwood-incident-archive/INC-2026-0421-77/) and snapshot current pod logs. We need full evidence.

james_engineer: grabbing pod logs now and streaming to incident bucket. command: `kubectl logs ws-54f7 -n inference --timestamps > /tmp/ws-54f7.log && aws s3 cp /tmp/ws-54f7.log s3://redwood-incident-archive/INC-2026-0421-77/`

alice_sre: confirmed several logs contain auth fragments up to 40 chars. Most appear truncated; some look like refresh tokens (short-lived).

sam_security: immediate mitigation: 1) Roll back LOG_LEVEL change to info on all inference-ws replicas. 2) Block suspicious source IP ranges at edge WAF. 3) Rotate service tokens and revoke active sessions. Who can roll back?

alice_sre: I can push rollback config now. Rolling to LOG_LEVEL=info across eu-west-2. ETA ~4m.

maria_oncall: Sam, legal, and custsuccess - decision tree: do we notify customers now or after scope?

irene_legal: Hold notifications until we complete quick scope and confirm which accounts affected. We need to avoid false alarms but prepare template. Legal on standby.

rachel_custsuccess: prepping customer-impact template. If tokens could be replayable we need a high-touch list. I'll compile account list once security hands over suspected accounts.

sam_security: Agreed. Immediate actions prioritized: rotation of infra service account keys (svc-inference-prod), revoke all active user sessions older than 10m, and issue short TTL for refreshes. Assigning owners: svc-rotate -> alice_sre, sessions-revoke -> maria_oncall, edge-block -> james_engineer.

alice_sre: starting service-account key rotate. Steps: 1) create new key in KMS-managed keystore 2) deploy new key to inference secrets 3) warm deploy 4) retire old key after 2h. Running `rdr-key rotate --service svc-inference-prod --env prod --label incident-0421`

maria_oncall: revoking sessions: `POST https://console.redwood.ai/admin/sessions/revoke` payload `{reason: "auth-log-leak-0421", age_seconds: 600}`. Executing now. Will monitor error rates.

james_engineer: edge WAF rule applied to block top 5 suspicious /24s. Confirmed reduced request volume from those sources by ~92%.

alice_sre: LOG_LEVEL set back to info on all pods. No new debug auth prints observed in the last 60s. Rolling restart finished.

sam_security: Good. Now forensic scope: which customers' tokens appear in logs? We found 17 token fragments that map to session IDs. Extracting session->account mapping from session-store.

alice_sre: returned mapping: 6 internal svc accounts, 11 end-customer sessions across 4 orgs (org-47, org-1022, org-214). Sharing obfuscated list in a secure thread (security channel).

rachel_custsuccess: Received obfuscated list. Planning high-touch outreach: org-1022 and org-214 need SOC call. Preparing comms.

irene_legal: Keep comms templated and do not admit scope beyond confirmed. We need to confirm whether plaintext PII was in logs — looks like only Authorization header fragments. Legal: high risk if any full tokens present.

sam_security: So far fragments only. However, we can't rule out that fragments could be reconstructed in combination with other telemetry. Recommend rotating customer-facing API keys for the 4 affected orgs and offering support.

maria_oncall: Customer-impact ETA: initial outreach to affected customers within next 90 minutes pending legal sign-off.

incident-bot: NOTE: runbook step triggered -> incident.state=mitigating, severity=sev2. Pager remains.

alice_sre: Completed service account rotation and deployed new secrets. Monitoring deployments for 15m.

james_engineer: Edge blocking causing some 401s from certain aggregator IPs — #observability shows spike in 401 but overall traffic back to baseline. Notifying partners if they call.

sam_security: Post-mitigation actions: 1) full audit of logging changes in last 7 days, 2) revert logging code path to safe formatter, 3) introduce automated lint/gate preventing auth headers in logs, 4) run synthetic replay to ensure no leakage. Assign owners: code-fix -> james_engineer, audit -> sam_security, lint-rule -> alice_sre.

rachel_custsuccess: Customer comms draft ready, pending legal review. Template includes: what happened, what we did, recommended customer actions (rotate keys, review sessions), and offer of SOC call.

irene_legal: Reviewing now. If approved will sign off for targeted disclosure.

maria_oncall: summary for postmortem: root cause = debug log rollout exposing Authorization header fragments via ws debug formatter during a rolling deploy. Mitigations executed: rollback, key rotation, session revoke, edge blocks, preserved logs.

sam_security: I'll schedule follow-up for extended forensics and potential regulatory notification assessment. Thanks all — keep this channel for updates only.

alice_sre: Recording all commands and artifacts to s3://redwood-incident-archive/INC-2026-0421-77/ and creating a ticket INFR-4721 for the code fix.

incident-bot: UPDATE: incident mitigated -> reduction in anomalous auth successes to baseline. Next: postmortem + customers. Closing pager in 2h unless escalated. :white_check_mark:
